driver-fault.comment: The events that report a refusal, a failure or an ending invocation. The list is the log call sites in drive.ts, not the plan's prose.

driver-event.comment: Every other event the loop logs: phase, run-started, run-resumed, instruction-issued, engine-invoked, engine-returned, interrupt-deferred, plan-accepted, report-accepted, check-passed, preverify, dispositions-accepted, dispute-recorded, run-of-record, landed. Matched by shape so a new event name is coloured the day it is added.

field.comment: The name and its equals sign recede; the value keeps the plain foreground, so 1/12 reads and invocation= does not.

session-complete.comment: The one dabbler: line that is not a fault -- the run finishing. Painting the happy ending in the error colour would teach the reader to ignore the colour.
session-complete.name: keyword.control.complete.dabbler-drive

diagnostic.comment: dabbler: refused ..., dabbler: STOPPED (...), dabbler: not inside a git repository, a bare dabbler: message, and the extension's own launch failure.
diagnostic.name: invalid.illegal.diagnostic.dabbler-drive

verify-verified.comment: The clean round. `dabbler verify` runs inside the drive and prints through this channel, so its verdict is one of the channel's line kinds -- and the most consequential one in the session.
verify-verified.name: keyword.control.verdict.dabbler-drive

verify-unreviewed.comment: Landed, and no verifier saw the repair. Neither a refusal nor a clean pass, and a reader who skims past it has missed the one line that says so.
verify-unreviewed.name: invalid.deprecated.verdict.dabbler-drive

verify-fault.comment: Everything else the verb prints: a blocking round, the cap reached unresolved, a refusal, a routed call that failed, a config or ledger error. The two lines above are the only benign ones it has, so this is a blanket rule after them rather than a list that would go stale -- the same shape the `dabbler:` diagnostics take.
verify-fault.name: invalid.illegal.verdict.dabbler-drive

engine.comment: The engine's own output, under the gutter the driver prints for it.

engine-aside.comment: Reasoning and tool results: the noisiest lines, and the ones a person skims past.
engine-aside.name: comment.line.aside.dabbler-drive

engine-keyword.comment: The invocation's own boundaries. `engine:` is deliberately absent: with no scope it keeps the plain foreground and is the brightest text in the block, which is where the engine speaks to a person.
engine-keyword.name: keyword.control.engine.dabbler-drive
